title: Called to Make a Difference — Isaiah 6:8
paragraphs: Called to Make a Difference — Isaiah 6:8
Some people keep waiting for a louder sign from God.

But the real problem is not that God is silent.
It is that too many hearts are still unavailable.

Isaiah did not step forward because he felt impressive. He stepped forward because he had been undone by holiness, cleansed by grace, and awakened to purpose. First came the vision. Then the breaking. Then the cleansing. And only then came the call: “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And Isaiah answered, “Here am I; send me.” (Isaiah 6:8)
That is how God still works.

He does not call the proud.
He calls the surrendered.

He does not send people who think they are enough.
He sends people who know they need mercy.

But here’s what we miss: making a difference is not about building your name. It is about offering your life to the One who already knows your weakness and still says, “Go.” The world celebrates talent. Heaven looks for yieldedness. The difference-makers in Scripture were not the most polished—they were the ones who said yes.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because our greatest qualification is not our strength.
It is the mercy of Christ.

Jesus is the better answer to Isaiah 6:8. He did not just say, “Send me.” He came. He entered our sin-stained world, carried our guilt to the cross, rose again in victory, and now calls redeemed people to live on mission. We are not sent to prove ourselves. We are sent because we belong to Him.

So today, stop asking, “Am I enough?”
Ask, “Lord, am I available?”

One surrendered yes can shake a family.
A city.
A generation.

Prayer:
Lord, here am I. Cleanse what is unclean. Break what is proud. Awaken what has grown cold. Use my life for Your glory, not mine. In Jesus’ name, amen.
